findings.text: `edit: "move"` is in the contract (SKILL.md:26, voice-assistant.md:341) but `Widget.Thread.place()` (Widget.js diff lines 269-290) ignores it, and `where: "up"` draws the same as `beside` (Widget.css only styles `inside`). Either say in the plan that move/up are the next brief, or drop them from the skill until they do something.

The plan says "a node check reads the session file and confirms every owner sentence appears exactly once" (voice-assistant.md:344), but the only coverage check is the browser one in test/in-place.mjs:493. That is fine for this slice; the plan should say so, or the node check should become its own item.

fixture/v-fixture.jsonl:5 has a `{place}` line stamped `voice-assistant-test` that in-place.mjs never reads (it keeps only `chat` lines, :426). Either drop the line or have the test apply it, so the fixture shows what it really tests.

Setting `MODES.dictate` to `{ bubble: true }` (Widget.js:132) changes every Dictate surface, not just voice. This is in line with ask 2b ("no text-area hop"), but it is the widest change in the diff. The 400 and 1200 proof only covers a bare Widget, not the ✦ sheet or the rail.

The new `live()` drops the `sent` parameter. Three callers still pass `sent: true` (ai/cards/card.js:260, ai/rail/rail.js:646, TimelineTalk.js:50). They appear to drive `ext/Chat`'s own `live()` (Chat.js:794), so nothing breaks, but someone should confirm that none of them reaches `Widget.Thread`.

SKILL.md:29 lets the assistant skip the write for `same`/`nothing`. That means "no line yet" and "decided same" look identical in the file, so a stalled assistant is invisible. A one-line `same` write is cheap and keeps every sentence accounted for.
I can't verify from the diff alone that each slice was its own commit through a worktree and `merge.mjs`, or that the card was updated. The diff arrives as one patch.
